lines.text: A point inside a rectangle, joined to all four corners.
lines.caption: A point inside a rectangle, joined to all four corners.

lines.text: Three triangle areas are known. Can you find the fourth, without knowing where the point is?
lines.caption: Three triangle areas are known. Can you find the fourth, without knowing where the point is?

lines.text: The bottom, right and top triangles have areas fifteen, twenty-two and twenty-five.
lines.caption: The bottom, right and top triangles have areas fifteen, twenty-two and twenty-five.

lines.text: What is the area of the left triangle?
lines.caption: What is the area of the left triangle?

lines.text: Look at the bottom and top triangles together. Their heights stack up to the full height.
lines.caption: Look at the bottom and top triangles together. Their heights stack up to the full height.

lines.text: So together, they make exactly HALF the rectangle!
lines.caption: So together, they make exactly HALF the rectangle!

lines.text: Fifteen plus twenty-five is forty. So the left and right pair must make forty too.
lines.caption: Fifteen plus twenty-five is forty. So the left and right pair must make forty too.

lines.text: Forty, take away twenty-two, is eighteen. The left triangle is eighteen, choice C!
lines.caption: Forty, take away twenty-two, is eighteen. The left triangle is eighteen, choice C!

lines.text: And the point can be anywhere. Opposite triangles always make half!
lines.caption: And the point can be anywhere. Opposite triangles always make half!

lines.text: Why is it always half? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why is it always half? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
